newsitem.title: USA: AMR Q1 results hurt by strike-related charge.
newsitem.headline: AMR Q1 results hurt by strike-related charge.

text.p: AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, said it took a $20 million charge in the first quarter for stock options awarded to its pilots as part of a tentative wage settlement.
AMR posted first quarter earnings of $1.65 per diluted share on total operating revenues of $4.4 billion, compared to earnings of $1.84 per diluted share on revenues of $4.3 billion last year.
American reached a tentative labor pact with its pilots two weeks ago, ending months of bitter negotiations.
The deal, if approved by the unions' members, averts the prospect of a second strike by the pilots union.
Last February 15, the pilots union went on strike but its members were sent almost immediately back to work by a Presidential Emergency Board created by President Clinton to resolve the dispute.
Although the strike was brief, American suffered as passengers booked away from American to avoid getting stranded by the strike.
"Despite the effects of a threatened pilot strike, strong levels of demand, combined with relatively limited capacity additions, produced good results for us," said AMR chairman Robert Crandall.
"While our results are testimony to the continuing strength of demand, they would have been dramatically better absent the labor dispute," Crandall said.

The proposed five-year labor agreement includes a nine percent wage increase, 5.75 million in stock options offered at $10 a share below market value and a compromise on American's plan to have pilots from its American Eagle subsidiary fly new regional jets the company plans to buy.
AMR confirmed that it will repurchase up to 5.75 million share of its common stock to offset the potential dilution from the pilot stock options.
The repurchase is contingent on the the rank-and-file pilot union members approving the tentative labor pact.
